tool_definitions.name: subagent
tool_definitions.description: start independent subagents with a shared optional system prompt and individual tasks, send a finished subagent a follow-up, and inspect or control them by name; at most 5 run at once; a subagent knows only a short description of its sandbox, your system_prompt, and its prompt: none of your instructions, context files or conversation reach it, so give it everything it needs; each subagent can read but not write its workspace, and has a shell only while you do, writing only to its own scratch, which is subagents/<name> inside your scratch but which it calls /tmp, so a /tmp path it reports may mean your /tmp/subagents/<name>/...; it cannot read the rest of your scratch, so put what it needs in its prompt, or, for a follow-up, write files into your /tmp/subagents/<name> and refer to them by the /tmp paths it sees; never trust an answer blindly: however confident, it is an unverified claim that may be wrong, miss part of its task, or describe checks it never ran, so before you act on it or pass it on, verify what matters yourself, such as by opening files it reports, rerunning key commands, or reading the code it cites; finished subagents whose answers you have not read through output report back after a short batching window; you are woken by them if you have ended your turn, so end your turn rather than waiting or polling for them

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: the subagents for status, output, or stop; empty means all of them

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the finished subagent to send a follow-up to (for send)

parameters.name: system_prompt
parameters.description: the only instructions every subagent shares, beside a short description of its sandbox (for start)

parameters.name: subagents

item_fields.name: prompt
item_fields.description: the whole task for this subagent, with whatever context it needs

item_fields.name: intent
item_fields.description: what this subagent is for, as a 5 to 7 word phrase opening with a capitalised -ing verb, such as "Reviewing the parser for missed errors"

item_fields.name: workspace
item_fields.description: the subagent's read-only workspace, any directory you can read; absent means yours

parameters.description: one task per independent subagent (for start)
